name: Design fracturing treatments
summary: Completions design engineers turn a producer's completion program for a pad into a stage-by-stage pump schedule: how much water, which fluid system and chemical loadings, how much sand of which mesh at which concentrations, at what rate and with what expected surface pressure. A technical sales engineer manages the request and the producer, a data analyst pulls offset well results, and the laboratory tests the producer's water against the chemical package. The work is slow because well data arrive incomplete, lab samples take days to reach Calgary, and producers send designs back for changes to tonnage, stage spacing or fluid choice, sometimes after the pad is already scheduled.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company with six to eight crewed frac fleets working multi-well pads in Alberta and northeast BC from district bases, with a Calgary engineering and sales office.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB pressure pumpers in 2019-2022: ERP, spreadsheets, email and phone, fracture modelling software and a data van acquisition system; no automated scheduling optimiser.

unit_of_work: one pad design (pump schedules for all wells on a pad)
trigger: A producer sends a completion program for a pad, either for an awarded pad under a master service agreement or as part of a tender.
end_state: A producer-approved design issued to frac operations, the treater and supply chain, or a tender design returned that the producer did not award.

volume.seasonality: Peaks in October to December when producers design winter programs and tender the next year's work; lower during spring break-up.

evidence.note: Kept the organisation file's 12-25-40 designs a month: about 18 executed pads a month plus tender designs and redesigns that are never pumped.
Request intake, costing and producer contact for about 25 designs a month; estimate.
About 20-30 engineering hours a pad design including peer review and revisions; the remaining engineers work on cement and coiled tubing programs and field support; estimate.
Offset well data pulls; estimate. Not listed among the organisation file's roles for this process.
Water compatibility and fluid performance tests for new water sources; estimate. Not listed among the organisation file's roles for this process.

systems.name: Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Fracture and cement placement modelling software
Laboratory test records (lab database and spreadsheets)
Data van acquisition and treatment monitoring system
Business intelligence dashboards on ERP and job data
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)

steps.name: Receive completion program
steps.description: The technical sales engineer receives the producer's completion program: well surveys, casing and wellhead ratings, completion type (plug and perf or sleeves), stage count and spacing, target tonnage per stage and fluid preference. The engineer logs it in the design tracker and checks whether anything needed for design is missing.

error.defect_description: Casing or wellhead rating not captured, so the design pressure limit is wrong

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Request missing well data
steps.description: The technical sales engineer emails the producer's completions engineer for the missing items, typically casing grade and weight, wellhead pressure rating, log data or the water source for the pad.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Wait for producer data
steps.description: The producer gathers the requested surveys, casing tallies or log files from its drilling and geology teams and sends them back.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Assign engineer and set design basis
steps.description: The lead design engineer assigns the pad to an engineer by area and workload and sets the design basis with them: the formation, the producer's previous designs, which offsets to study and the target treatment size.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Pull offset well results
steps.description: The completions data analyst queries the company's job database and public well data for offset wells in the same formation and area, extracts treating pressures, rates, tonnage per stage, screen-outs and public chemical disclosures, and builds an offset table for the engineer.

error.defect_description: Offsets from a different formation or completion type included

evidence.note: Fracture design draws on formation-specific frac databases (src1); times are estimates.

steps.name: Request water sample and lab tests
steps.description: If the pad uses a new water source or recycled produced water, the design engineer asks the producer to ship a water sample and writes a lab request for friction reducer performance, crosslink or viscosity tests and scale tendency with the proposed chemical package.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Run water compatibility tests
steps.description: When the sample arrives a laboratory technologist runs water analysis, friction loop or viscosity tests with candidate friction reducers or gels at the planned loadings, checks for scale and bacteria issues, and records results in the lab database.

error.defect_description: Sample mislabelled or aged, so results do not represent the pad water

evidence.note: Full-service lab testing and fluid system support (src1); times are estimates.

steps.name: Build the model and pump schedule
steps.description: The engineer enters well geometry, rock properties from logs and offsets, perforation clusters and fluid properties into fracture modelling software, runs stage designs and settles water volume, pumping rate, proppant ramp by concentration, pad and flush volumes and predicted surface pressure for each stage.

error.defect_description: Wrong friction or rock inputs, so predicted pressure is too low

evidence.note: Fracture models combined with geological and geophysical data (src1); time is an estimate.

steps.name: Select chemicals and loadings
steps.description: Using lab results or past jobs on the same water, the engineer picks the friction reducer or gel system, breaker, biocide, scale inhibitor, surfactant and clay control, sets loadings per cubic metre and checks products for compatibility and the producer's approved product list.

evidence.note: Fluid system families (src1); time is an estimate.

steps.name: Check pressure limits and offset risk
steps.description: The engineer compares the maximum predicted treating pressure with casing burst, wellhead and frac tree ratings using the company safety factor, and lists offset wells the producer has flagged for interwellbore communication risk so the producer can plan monitoring or shut-ins.

control.basis: AER Directive 083 (licensee duty to manage wellbore integrity and offset well risk, with service company input) and IRP 24 fracture stimulation hazard management

evidence.note: Directive 083 scope (src9) and IRP 24 hazard management (src10); time is an estimate.

steps.name: Peer review the design
steps.description: A senior design engineer checks the model inputs, pump schedule totals, chemical loadings and pressure check against offsets and the producer's past results, and either signs off or returns specific corrections.

control.basis: Company engineering peer review before a design leaves the office

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Estimate job cost
steps.description: The technical sales engineer prices the design from the customer's price book: pumping charges by stage or hour, horsepower, proppant by tonne, chemicals by litre, fuel and mobilization, and checks the total against the producer's budget expectations.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Draft the design proposal
steps.description: The engineer assembles the proposal: pump schedule tables per stage, fluid and chemical program, predicted pressures and horsepower requirement, material totals per well and pad, and the offset comparison, in the standard Word and Excel template.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Send design to producer
steps.description: The technical sales engineer reviews the package for commercial wording, sends it to the producer's completions engineer and sets up a review call if the design departs from the producer's program.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Wait for producer review
steps.description: The producer's completions team reviews the design, often comparing it with other pumpers' proposals, and accepts it, asks for changes to tonnage, stage spacing, fluid or rate, or, for tender designs, awards the work elsewhere.

next.condition: tender not awarded or pad dropped

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Revise design for producer comments
steps.description: The engineer reruns the affected stages with the requested changes, updates totals, pressures and the chemical program, and returns the revision with a short note of what changed.

error.defect_description: Totals not updated everywhere after a change

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Finalize and issue approved design
steps.description: The engineer locks the approved revision in the document store, records the version, and issues it to frac operations planning, the field supervisor and treater, and supply chain for material totals.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Prepare treater job plan and acquisition file
steps.description: The engineer exports the pump schedule into the data van's job template and writes the treater's job plan: stage sequence, rate and concentration steps, pressure limits and kickout settings, and what to do on a pressure spike or screen-out.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Hold technical handover with treater
steps.description: The engineer walks the treater and field supervisor through the design and job plan by phone or video call, answers questions about expected pressures and diversion, and notes any field concerns.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Wait for producer's late change
steps.description: Close to or during the job the producer changes stage count, tonnage or fluid after reviewing new drilling results or offset performance, and sends the change by email.

evidence.note: Producer-driven changes and client location delays reported by STEP (src2); share is an estimate.

steps.name: Revise for the late change
steps.description: The engineer reruns the affected stages in the modelling software, checks the new maximum pressure against casing and wellhead limits again, and updates material totals and the treater job plan.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Reissue revised design
steps.description: The engineer issues the new revision with a change note to operations, the treater and supply chain, and asks the coordinator to adjust material orders.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

exceptions.name: Incomplete well data
exceptions.description: Casing, wellhead or survey data missing from the program and requested from the producer.

exceptions.name: New water source
exceptions.description: Lab compatibility testing on a shipped water sample before chemicals are chosen.

exceptions.name: Producer changes
exceptions.description: Producer asks for different tonnage, spacing or fluid; one or more revision rounds.

exceptions.name: Late change near the job
exceptions.description: Producer changes the design after it was issued, sometimes after rig-up.

exceptions.name: Tender design not used
exceptions.description: Design prepared for a tender that the company did not win, or a pad the producer dropped.

benchmarks.unit: days from completion program received to approved design issued and handed over to the treater

evidence.note: Estimate: one to two weeks of engineering and producer review plus a few days to hand over to the field is common; long tails from producer review cycles and lab sample transit.

pain_points.description: Producer review cycles and late changes force reruns and reissues, and the change must then be chased into material orders and the treater's plan.

evidence.note: Customer-driven changes noted by STEP (src2); frequency estimated.

pain_points.description: Water samples travel by courier to the Calgary lab, adding days before chemicals can be confirmed.

evidence.note: Central full-service lab in Calgary (src1); transit time estimated.

pain_points.description: Offset data are pulled by hand from several databases into spreadsheets for each design.

evidence.note: Typical 2019-2022 practice.

sources.title: Trican - Hydraulic fracturing
sources.supports: Engineering team works with customers on program design, MiniFrac analysis, pore and closure pressure; fracture design combines fracture models with geological and geophysical data and formation frac databases; slickwater, HVFR, crosslinked, foam and other fluid systems; full-service lab in Calgary; logistical planning for chemicals, proppants, people and equipment; Tier 4 dynamic gas blending pumps.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Canadian fracturing: 977 operating days in 2021 and 704 in 2020 with 4 and 3 crews; 1,012,000 tonnes of proppant in 2021; weather delays in late December 2021 and extreme cold in January 2022; extended delays on a client location from well conditions; work moved between quarters; spring break-up conditions restrict operations; smaller jobs and single-well work less efficient than multi-well pads.

sources.title: Directive 083: Hydraulic Fracturing - Subsurface Integrity
sources.supports: Requirements for managing subsurface integrity during fracturing: wellbore integrity, well control at offset wells, protection of nonsaline aquifers and water wells; notification through OneStop; communication events with offset wells reported to the AER. Page describes the current edition; earlier editions applied in 2019-2022.

sources.title: DACC IRP Volume 24: Fracture Stimulation
sources.supports: Industry recommended practice for managing subject well integrity, interwellbore communication and surface operations during fracture stimulation, built on a Fracture Stimulation Hazard Management Process and a shared hazard register (2016 edition in force in 2019-2022).

assumptions: Loaded hourly costs are taken from the organisation file.
All cases start from a producer's completion program; about 30 percent are tender designs that pass through the tender response team, which the organisation file does not link to this process.
Offset well identification for Directive 083 is the licensee's duty; the service company's step is to check pressure limits and flag offsets the producer lists.
The completions data analyst and laboratory technologist are organisation file roles that the process_map entry does not list.
Lab tests are counted here only when a new water source needs them; routine proppant and chemical quality testing is a separate process.
